topic: Halloween in Korea: English academy parties, apartment trick-or-treat by sign-up, store goods, theme park zombies, club streets, Itaewon 2022 and crowd control
title: In Korea, Halloween Starts at English School

slides.kicker: NO PORCH LIGHTS. NO CANDY BOWLS.
slides.headline: In Korea, Halloween **starts at English school.**
slides.note: Costumes in class, candy by sign-up, zombies after dark.

slides.headline: It came in **through the classroom**
slides.body: English academies (영어학원) and kindergartens throw costume parties in late October. For many Koreans, that was their first Halloween.

slides.headline: Trick-or-treat **by sign-up**
slides.body: Some apartment complexes run it as an event. Homes that join put a sign on the door, and kids only knock where they see one.

slides.headline: The shops go **orange**
slides.body: By early October, budget stores and convenience stores fill up with pumpkin buckets, witch hats and devil-horn headbands.

slides.headline: Theme parks **bring zombies**
slides.body: Big theme parks turn into horror zones every fall. After dark, actors in zombie makeup chase screaming guests down the streets.

slides.headline: Adults head **for the club streets**
slides.body: Hongdae and Itaewon filled with costumes on the weekend before October 31. It became a young-adult party night.

slides.headline: Then **one night changed it**
slides.body: On October 29, 2022, a crowd crush in a narrow Itaewon alley turned Halloween weekend into a time of mourning.

slides.headline: Lives lost **that night**
slides.body: Now police manage crowds every October, and many people celebrate in smaller places.

slides.headline: Elsewhere a night at the door. **Here, an event.**
slides.body: In many countries Halloween means knocking on neighbors' doors. In Korea, it is something you plan, join or book.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: Warm Seoul apartment hallway at night with a small carved pumpkin lantern by a door, softly blurred behind the text.

caption:
In Korea, Halloween didn't arrive on doorsteps. It came through English classrooms, theme parks and club streets.

And since 2022, it's celebrated more carefully.

How do you spend Halloween where you live?
reply: One more: for a lot of Koreans in their 20s and 30s, the first Halloween they ever had was in a hagwon classroom, wearing a costume their mom bought that week. What was your first Halloween like?
fact_check: 2장: 영어학원·영어유치원 핼러윈 파티가 국내 확산 통로라는 것은 통설(언론 다수). 'for many Koreans'로 표기.
3장: 아파트 단지 핼러윈 행사 — 참여 세대가 문 앞에 표시, 표시된 집만 방문. 'some apartment complexes'로 한정.
4장: 다이소·편의점 핼러윈 용품(호박 바구니, 마녀 모자, 머리띠). 매장명 쓰지 않음.
5장: 에버랜드 블러드시티, 롯데월드 핼러윈 좀비 행사 등. 'big theme parks'로 표기.
8장: 사망자 159명(정부 공식). 이후 경찰·지자체 핼러윈 인파 관리 대책 매년 시행.
9장: 일반화 비교, 특정국 단정 안 함.
